title: AI Sell-Off: Buy ANET, TSM & MU to Make Up for NVIDIA Losses - TradingView
content: The artificial intelligence (AI) trade is facing one of its toughest tests yet. After driving Wall Street's rally for much of 2026, technology and semiconductor stocks have come under intense selling pressure as investors question lofty valuations, the sustainability of hyperscaler capital expenditures and the time required to monetize massive AI investments. Rising inflation, higher Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding data-center construction have added to the pressure. The weakness is also evident in AI-focused ETFs. Over the past 30 days, the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) has declined 11.4%, while the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) has plunged 17.1%, entering correction territory. ARTY's steeper decline indicates the extent of selling pressure across companies positioned to benefit from future AI adoption. The Nov. 5 sell-off was particularly severe. The iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX plunged 12.1%. The pressure escalated on Nov. 8 following a corporate governance controversy involving NVIDIA NVDA. NVIDIA shares fell 4.27% on Nov. 9 as concerns over leadership continuity, board oversight and potential national-security implications weighed on investor sentiment. The sell-off deepened on Nov. 10, with NVIDIA losing another 6.5% and the Nasdaq Composite declining 1%. Broader concerns over AI infrastructure spending, complications surrounding a major Ohio data-center project and hotter-than-expected inflation further undermined technology stocks. However, does this correction signal the end of the AI investment opportunity, or is it creating an attractive entry point in fundamentally strong companies? Let's find out. Here, we have picked three AI stocks — Arista Networks ANET, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM or TSMC and Micron Technology MU — all carrying favorable Zacks Rank and having strong fundamentals, making them attractive alternatives to NVIDIA for investors seeking AI exposure beyond the market leader amid the current volatility. Why Quality AI Stocks Beyond NVIDIA Are Attractive Now Despite the correction, long-term AI infrastructure demand remains strong. According to IDC's Nov. 6 report, global AI infrastructure spending reached $121.4 billion in the second quarter, up 53.3% year over year. IDC raised its 2026 spending forecast to $521 billion from $497 billion previously and expects the market to reach $1.17 trillion by 2029. Notably, non-accelerated, CPU-based infrastructure spending grew 61.1%, outpacing the 52.2% growth in accelerated systems, highlighting expanding investment opportunities beyond GPU suppliers. Meanwhile, J.P. Morgan projected AI capital expenditure of approximately $900 billion in 2026, although financing, electricity availability and semiconductor supply remain constraints. This spending creates opportunities beyond NVIDIA across AI networking, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, high-bandwidth memory and computing processors. Investors should focus on companies translating AI demand into measurable revenue growth and stronger earnings rather than speculative AI exposure. Arista: It is benefiting from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet networking in AI data centers. Its third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 58.5% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS increased to $1.20 from 77 cents a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $3.9-$4 billion. ANET's networking exposure makes it an attractive means to participate in AI infrastructure expansion beyond chip manufacturing. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings indicates growth of 45.6% on current-year sales growth of 47.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for ANET have been revised upward by 4.3% to $4.36 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. Taiwan Semiconductor: TSMC's advanced manufacturing capabilities make it indispensable to the AI semiconductor ecosystem. Its October 2026 revenues jumped 59.7% year over year. Its January-October 2026 revenues increased 43.3% to NT$4.49 trillion. TSMC offers exposure to AI demand across multiple chip designers, rather than relying on a single GPU manufacturer. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings suggests 63.9% growth, while sales are expected to increase 40.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for TSM have been revised upward by 2.3% to $17.46 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1. Micron: The AI expansion is increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced DRAM, positioning Micron favorably. The company reported strong fiscal fourth quarter 2026 revenues of $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier. Micron has also commenced high-volume shipments of HBM4. The consensus estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings suggests growth of 133.1%. Sales are expected to surge 110%. Over the past 60 days, fiscal 2027 earnings estimates for MU have been revised upward by 11.5% to $176.04 per share. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). The AI revolution has already minted millionaires. But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important? Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about TSMC (TSM). TSMC currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.21, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 19 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.21 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy. Of the 19 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and two are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 84.2% and 10.5% of all recommendations. Check price target & stock forecast for TSMC here>>> While the ABR calls for buying TSMC, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential. Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations. In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement. Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision. In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures. Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5. Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide. On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements. Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns. There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices. Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for TSMC, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 5.2% over the past month to $17.46. Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for TSMC. Rather than designing its own branded processors for disposal, it fabricates the chips that others design, turning blueprints into finished silicon across a vast network of fabrication plants. Advanced packaging has moved from a technical footnote to a defining pillar of artificial intelligence hardware. The foundry's packaging techniques sit at the heart of this shift. title: TSM Stock: October Revenue Up 59.7%, Ahead of Q4 Pace - FinanceFeeds
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) reported record monthly revenue of NT$586.89 billion, approximately $17.88 billion at the exchange rate cited by InvestingCube, for October 2026. The result represents a 59.7% increase from a year earlier and a 14.7% rise from September, providing fresh evidence of strong semiconductor demand following last week’s sharp selloff in AI-related stocks. TSM stock traded at $394.19, up 1.43%, at 11:22 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, according to ChartExchange. The American depositary receipts had closed Monday at $388.62, gaining 3.51%, after a particularly volatile week that included a 10.78% decline on November 5. The October revenue figure is the first monthly reading for TSMC’s fourth quarter, which runs through December. It puts the company ahead of the average monthly revenue pace implied by its October 15 guidance of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. The result is also relevant to investors watching Nvidia, which reports quarterly earnings on November 17. In its November 10 revenue announcement, TSMC reported October consolidated sales of NT$586.89 billion, compared with NT$511.86 billion in September and NT$367.47 billion in October 2025. The increase of approximately NT$75 billion from September pushed monthly revenue above the previous record of NT$514.81 billion set in August. October was also the first month in which TSMC generated more than NT$580 billion in sales. For January through October, consolidated revenue reached NT$4,485.62 billion, increasing 43.3% from NT$3,130.44 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. October’s 59.7% annual growth exceeded the 43.3% growth recorded over the first ten months. The acceleration is consistent with the company’s previous commentary about strong demand for leading-edge manufacturing, although the monthly release does not identify how much revenue came specifically from AI processors, smartphone chips or other products. The sequential increase is particularly notable because September had already remained close to August’s record. FinanceFeeds previously reported that TSMC’s September revenue reached NT$511.9 billion, up 54.6% year over year, leaving the company operating near its highest recorded monthly sales level. October’s result moves substantially beyond that level, suggesting that the fourth quarter has begun with stronger revenue momentum than the preceding quarter’s final month. The latest revenue number can be compared directly with the outlook management provided during its October 15 earnings announcement. In its third-quarter earnings release, TSMC projected fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, based on an exchange-rate assumption of NT$31.8 per US dollar. That guidance translates to approximately NT$1.663 trillion to NT$1.727 trillion. After October’s NT$586.89 billion, TSMC would need combined revenue of approximately NT$1.076 trillion to NT$1.140 trillion across November and December to reach the original target range. That works out to an average of roughly NT$538.1 billion to NT$569.9 billion per month over the remaining two months. October exceeded even the upper-end monthly requirement by approximately NT$17 billion. If November and December each matched October’s revenue, fourth-quarter sales would reach approximately NT$1.761 trillion, above the New Taiwan dollar equivalent of the company’s original guidance ceiling. This is a comparison using TSMC’s assumed guidance exchange rate, not a revised forecast or a confirmed earnings beat. Actual reported dollar revenue will depend on the company’s financial reporting and exchange-rate treatment during the quarter. October’s roughly $17.88 billion equivalent, calculated using a different exchange rate, should not be mixed directly with the guidance conversion. The company also forecast fourth-quarter gross margin of 65% to 67% and operating margin of 56.5% to 58.5%. Revenue alone cannot establish whether TSMC will meet those profitability targets, especially as it expands advanced manufacturing capacity. FinanceFeeds’ October 15 analysis of TSMC’s third-quarter results examined the company’s $46.72 billion quarterly revenue, 66.4% gross margin and outlook for accelerating sales. TSMC’s October figures arrive after a difficult period for semiconductor stocks. Its US-listed shares fell 10.78% on November 5, closing at $353.10, before recovering 6.33% on Friday and another 3.51% on Monday. The rebound followed concerns about AI infrastructure investment, capital spending and potential delays in data center development. Those concerns had weighed on several companies involved in advanced computing, even as their reported financial performance remained strong. TSMC’s monthly sales figures provide a more direct indication of manufacturing activity. The company produces advanced processors for customers including Nvidia, AMD and Apple, while also supplying chips for custom AI accelerators and other high-performance computing applications. Its third-quarter technology mix showed the growing importance of advanced production nodes. Chips manufactured using 2-nanometer technology accounted for 8% of wafer revenue, while 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer processes contributed 33% and 28%, respectively. Technologies at 7 nanometers and below accounted for 79% of total wafer revenue. TSMC CFO Wendell Huang said during the October earnings announcement that fourth-quarter performance would benefit from continued demand for leading-edge technologies, including the rapid expansion of 2-nanometer production. However, stronger manufacturing revenue does not necessarily establish that every AI customer is increasing its orders at the same rate. TSMC’s monthly report does not disclose customer-level sales, shipment volumes by technology or the contribution of changes in pricing. Profitability also remains a consideration. Management has previously identified margin pressure associated with the introduction of 2-nanometer technology and the higher operating costs of overseas manufacturing facilities. Investors will need the full quarterly results to determine how much of the additional revenue translates into profit. TSMC’s October revenue announcement comes one week before Nvidia’s next earnings report, making the manufacturing data particularly relevant to expectations for the AI accelerator market. Nvidia confirmed that it will release its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, with an earnings conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The reporting period ended October 25. RelatedAdvanced Micro Devices Closes at $649.42, Up 2.80%, After Lisa Su Says Supply Still Trails FinanceFeeds previously examined the upcoming announcement in its November 5 Nvidia stock analysis following the semiconductor selloff, highlighting concerns about data center construction and the durability of AI infrastructure spending. TSMC’s results provide evidence that demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing remained strong in October, but they cannot independently predict Nvidia’s revenue or earnings. The companies operate at different points in the supply chain, and manufacturing revenue does not necessarily correspond to sales recognized by Nvidia during the same reporting period. Investors will be watching Nvidia’s data center revenue, its forward guidance and management’s comments on accelerator demand, production capacity and customer spending. Those disclosures should offer another perspective on whether the industry’s strong manufacturing activity is continuing to translate into revenue growth for chip designers. For TSM stock, the next milestone will be the November revenue release, which will show whether October’s record was sustainable. November and December need to average approximately NT$570 billion to reach the upper end of the company’s existing fourth-quarter revenue target under its original exchange-rate assumption. October’s NT$586.89 billion provides a strong start and reduces the monthly revenue pace required for the remainder of the quarter. The remaining questions concern whether manufacturing demand can sustain that level and whether TSMC can preserve its projected margins while expanding its most advanced production technologies. title: Why Is TSM Stock Rising Overnight? - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) shares rose 1% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday after the Taiwanese contract chipmaker reported a sharp increase in monthly sales. Gains were tempered by controversy surrounding Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy, as well as a report speculating that the AI chipmaker is slowing chip orders. The go-to chipmaker for Nvidia and Apple (AAPL) said its October revenue rose 60% to NT$586.9 billion ($17.9 billion). That compares to the 51% growth pace in September quarter and 63% growth analysts polled by Bloomberg expect in the current quarter. Although TSMC’s upbeat monthly update is a bullish signal for the chip trader, semiconductor stocks were mixed in early Tuesday hours. NVDA shares were 1% higher after a sharp slide on Monday, while Intel (INTC) was up 0.3% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was down 0.4%. Nvidia is said to be considering slowing chip orders, which would affect upstream supply chain players like TSMC and ASE Technology Holding, a Taiwanese chip assembly and packaging firm, according to a report in the Taiwanese outlet Commercial Times. AMD could be a potential beneficiary. The developments come amid a volatile period of chip stocks. Last week, TSM fell sharply in tandem with other semiconductor stocks after Democrats, seen to be pro-regulation for AI and data centers, won both the Senate and House in the midterm elections. TSM stock is now down about 20% from its peak in early October. Nvidia CEO Huang on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a person U.S. authorities suspect to be a Chinese spy. The admission has created a financial shock, with investors panicking that Huang, a key force behind the AI boom, might lose his CEO title. On Monday, a law firm filed a class action lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang for misleading investors and Delaware senator Chris Coons called for a congressional investigation on national security grounds. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TSM remained ‘neutral’ for a second day. “$TSM Oct monthly rev drove past expectations. Set a new Oct record $SOXX $SOXL,” a trader wrote. On the news report regarding slowing orders, a trader wrote: Nvidia may cut its H200 chip orders at $TSM due to the Jensen scandal. H200's primarily go to China. Spare capacity freed up dues to Nvidia cancellations to be gobbled up by AMD and AVGO.” Certaines données de marché sont fournies par ICE Data Services. title: TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung: Asian Chip Stocks Rise Even As Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Controversy Tests Investor Confidence - TradingView
content: Asian chip stocks rose on Monday, alongside modest overnight gains in some U.S. semiconductor shares, marking a recovery after a selloff last week over fears that a Democrat-led Congress would slow the buildout of AI data centers. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shares in Taiwan ended 4.7% higher on Monday. Shares of Samsung and SK Hynix in Seoul gave up their gains from earlier in the day but still ended up 0.6% and 0.4% higher. To be sure, SK Hynix’s U.S. stock SKHY, and TSM were down 3.5% and 0.3% respectively in overnight trading. Among the key triggers on Monday was the controversy engulfing Nvidia. Over the weekend, CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with a person U.S. authorities suspect to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia said it launched an investigation into the issues, even as analysts debated the potential fallout. NVDA stock plunged 5.7% in overnight trading ahead of Monday. Some analysts believe that the incident could have far reaching consequences, including a near-term overhang on NVDA stock and Huang ultimately losing his CEO title. South Korean chip stocks were hit by the global sell-off in AI and semiconductor shares last week. Investors worried that a new U.S. Congress could impose tighter rules on AI data-center construction, potentially slowing the buildout and weakening future demand for the memory chips that Samsung and SK Hynix supply. The selling then fed on itself: overseas investors pulled money from the market, and Samsung and SK Hynix – two of the KOSPI’s biggest stocks – took the brunt. By the week’s close on Nov. 6, the KOSPI had fallen about 11.7%. Investors are expected to closely track updates around the Nvidia controversy, including a potential congressional investigation. Meanwhile, TSMC’s monthly sales update, due on Tuesday at 1:30 p.m. Taipei time, will also be in focus. TSMC reported record third-quarter profit that beat estimates and projected a 58% jump in current quarter sales.
